 JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.6392/2018 That on 03.06.2018 at about 6.00 p.m, when the Petitioner was proceeding as a passenger in an Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA03AF2911 and when the said autorickshaw reached near T.C. Palya main road, opposite Doddamma Temple, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the said Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA03AF2911 driven the same in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle and toppled down on the road.
Due to the said incident, the Petitioner fell down and had sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to General hospital, K.R. Puram,
wherein first aid was given and thereafter he was shifted to Bowring and Lady Curzen hospital,
wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
He had spent about Rs.1,50,000/ towards medical expenses and Rs.20,000/ towards food and nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as Coolie and was earning 15,000/ per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is permanently disabled and he lost his future employment.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA03 AF2911 by its driver.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its detailed Objection Statement.

6. The Respondent No.2 in its detailed Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.6392/2018 Petitioner and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.

Further it contended that the driver of the offending vehicle Raju vs Kashi on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66348017/
2 was not having valid and effective driving license and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner and has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

7. On the rival Pleadings, my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries due to RTA alleged to have been occurred on 03.06.2018 at about 6.00 p.m., near T.C. Palya main road,
opposite Doddamma Temple, due to the rash and negligent driving of Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA03AF2911?
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
8. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 13 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P10 and Ex.P13 to 15.
Further, he examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.11 and 12 and closed his side evidence.

On the other hand,
the Respondent No.2 has examined two witnesses as RW.1 and 2 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.R1 to 3 and closed its side evidence.

9. The learned counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied on the following decision:
1. MFA No.3297/2019 (MVD), in between Smt. Adilakshmamma & others Vs. Raju & another SCCH 15 7 MVC No.6392/2018 10.

sentences.text:
Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the written Arguments filed by the Petitioner and depositions, documents exhibited, the citation relied on and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order, for the following :

REASONS 11. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Autorickshaw Raju vs Kashi on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66348017/
3 bearing Reg.No.KA03AF2911 by its driver.

12. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the SCCH 15 8 MVC No.6392/2018 offending Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA03AF2911 by its driver.

13. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 13 documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10 and Ex.P13 to 15 and he has reiterated the Petition averments in his Chiefaffidavit.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P7 are the True copies of FIR with Complaint, Spot mahazar with Sketch, Wound certificate, Charge sheet, Discharge summary and Medical bills.
Ex.P8 is the Outpatient record.
Ex.P9 is the Aadhaar card.
Ex.P10 is the Medical bills.
Ex.P13 to 15 are the Xrays.

14. Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P 1 is the True copy of the FIR with Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one V. Rajesh, the K.R. Puram Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the offending Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA 03AF2911 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC and U/S SCCH 15 9 MVC No.6392/2018 185 of IMV Act.
Ex.P.2 is the true copy of Spot Mahazar with Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.

Ex.P.3 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner which shows the following injuries:
1) Deep cut wound 5 X 2 X 5cm mid 3rd lateral thigh 2) Fracture left elbow 15.
As per the opinion of the Doctor, injury No.2 is simple and injury No.1 is grievous in nature.

Ex.P.4 is the True copy of the Charge sheet which has been submitted by the Sub Inspector of Police,
K.R. Puram Traffic Police Station against the driver of the offending Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA 03AF2911 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC and U/s 3(1), 181, 185, 5, 180 and U/s 190(2) of IMV Act.
16.
Upon going through the Chargesheet i.e., Ex

. P4, Column No.17 reads as under :

Ex.P.5 is the Discharge summar?
 y of the Petitioner.
Ex.P6 is the Medical bills.

Further, the Petitioner got examined Doctor by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.11 and 12.
SCCH 15 11 MVC No.6392/2018 18.
P.W.1 is subjected for crossexamination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.
But nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.

To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Senior Manager by name Vinay Kumar as RW.1 and also examined another witness by name Nithyananda, FDA, RTO, K.R. Puram, Bengaluru as RW.2 and got marked in total 3 documents at Ex.R1 to 3 i.e., Authorisation letters and Copy of Policy and nothing has been elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1 in their crossexamination.
Charge sheet is the material document which was submitted by the I.O after thorough investigation.

Hence,
the Petitioner has proved that the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA03AF2911 by its driver and due to the said accident, he had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative".
SCCH 15 12 MVC No.6392/2018 19. Issue No.2:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending auto by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
20. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 24 years.

Further, in the Aadhar card i.e.,
Ex.P9, date of birth of the Petitioner was shown as 04.02.1993.
The accident took place on 03.06.2018.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 26 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
21. Further, the Petitioner has averred that, he was working as Cooli and Mortar work and was earning 15,000/ per month.
But, he has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.12,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.

Raju vs Kashi on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66348017/
5 SCCH 15 13 MVC No.6392/2018 22.
With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :
23.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P3 issued by the Medical Officer of the General hospital, K.R.
Puram, Bengaluru shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1) Deep cut wound 5 X 2 X 5cm mid 3rd lateral thigh 2) Fracture left elbow 24.
As per the opinion of the Doctor, injury No.2 is simple and injury No.1 is grievous in nature.
25. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding SCCH 15 14 MVC No.6392/2018 compensation of 30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
26. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of 20,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
27.
The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he had taken inpatient treatment at Comfort Multispeciality Hospital.
Upon going through Ex.P.5  Discharge summary of Comfort Multispeciality Hospital which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 07.06.2018 to 08.06.2018.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 02 days.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as one month.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 12,500/ under this head (@ 12,500/ per month ).
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE:

29. Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and Raju vs Kashi on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66348017/

entities.text: Raju vs Kashi on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6 nourishment and for his conveyance

. In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of 3,000/ (@ 100/ per day) towards attendants charges, 3,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and 3,000/ towards conveyance would be just SCCH 15 16 MVC No.6392/2018 and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 9,000/ under this head.
V.COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
30. The petitioner has stated in his evidence that, he had spent Rs.1,50,000/ towards medical and other incidental charges.

In order to prove this fact, he has produced 17 medical bills and hospital bills which are marked at Ex.P6 &
10.
I have gone through the medical bills.
The acceptable medical bills comes to Rs.65,802/.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at Rs.65,900/.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.65,900/ under this head.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:
31.

The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident,
he has suffered permanent SCCH 15 17 MVC No.6392/2018 disability and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

32. Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.2 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by him at Comfort Multi Speciality hospital.
Further, he assessed the whole body disability at 16%.
PW.2 got marked Clinical notes and Xray as per Ex.P11 and 12.
In the crossexamination, he admitted that, he is not the treated doctor.

Further he stated that, he examined the Petitioner only for assessment of disability and he has not gone through the previous medical record of the Petitioner and did not get opinion of the treated doctors while at the time of assessment of disability.
Further he stated that the fracture is united.

Having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the SCCH 15 18 MVC No.6392/2018 disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 8% would be just and proper.
33. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 17.

With multiplier of 17, income of 12,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 8%, the loss of future income comes to 2,04,000/ (12,500/ x 12 = 1,50,000/, 1,50,000/x 17 x 8/100 =
2,04,000/).

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 2,04,000/
under this head.

Raju vs Kashi on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66348017/
7

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
34.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000 /
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/
3. Loss of income during the laid  12,500/ SCCH 15 19 MVC No.6392/2018 up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  9,000/ and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses  65,900/
6. Loss of Future Income 2,04,000/ Total 3,41,400/
35.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 3,41,400/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

36. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Offending Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA03AF2911.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.

The Respondent No.2 has examined its Senior Manager as RW.1 and he got marked the copy of Policy at SCCH 15 20 MVC No.6392/2018 Ex.R2 which shows that the policy of the offending vehicle was valid at the time of accident.
37. It is the contention of the Respondent No.2 that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess Driving license at the time of accident.

In this regard the Respondent No.2 has examined one witness by name Nithyananda, FDA, RTO,
K.R.Puram, Bengaluru as RW.2 and he has deposed that, the address " Sundar S/o Nataraj, R/at No.47/4, 3rd Cross, 1st main, Anandapura, T.C. Palya, Bengaluru,"
comes to jurisdiction of their RTO.
Since, the date of birth and license number of the said Sundar has not provided, he could not in a position to say that the DL was issued to the said person or not from their RTO.
In the crossexamination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2, he denied the suggestion that since they have not issued said DL, they did not get the particulars of DL of the said person.
It is to be noted here that, the Learned Counsel for the Petitioner did not choose to cross examine RW.1

It is to be noted here that in this case the SCCH 15 21 MVC No.6392/2018 Charge sheet was also filed by the I.O against the driver of the offending auto for the offences punishable U/s 3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act for not holding DL at the time of accident.
Though, the summons served to the Respondent No.1, he remained absent and he was placed exparte.

Therefore, the Respondent No.1 Raju vs Kashi on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66348017/
8 being the owner of the said vehicle has failed to provide DL particulars of the driver of the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

38. In the decision reported in 2004(3) SCC 297 in between National Insurance Co.
Ltd., Vs. Swarn Singh and others, wherein, the Hon'ble Appex Court has pleased to held that the Tribunal can direct that the insurer is liable to be reimbursed by the insured for the compensation and other amounts which has been compelled to pay the third party under the award of the Tribunal.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co.
Ltd., Vs. Swarn Singh and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Appex Court has highlighted the concept of pay and recovery.

It is a settled law that where the driver does not possess a valid driving licence,
the insurer would still have to satisfy the compensation and thereafter to recover the said amount from the owner.

Hence, by relying on the above said dictum of Hon'ble Appex Court, this Tribunal is of the opinion that at the first instance, it is necessary to direct the insurer i.e., Respondent No.2 to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner and thereafter, recover the same from the Respondent No.1 i.e., insured.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
40. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

SCCH 15 23 MVC No.6392/2018  The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 3,41,400/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification.

The remaining 25% award amount shall be Raju vs Kashi on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66348017/
9 deposited as F.D. in the name of the SCCH 15 24 MVC No.6392/2018 Petitioner in any Nationalized or Schedule bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.

With multiplier of 17, income of 12,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 8%, the loss of future income comes to 2,04,000/ (12,500/ x 12 = 1,50,000/, 1,50,000/x 17 x 8/100 =
2,04,000/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 2,04,000/

40. Issue No.3:
In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
SCCH 15 23 MVC No.6392/2018  The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 3,41,400/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be Raju vs Kashi on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66348017/
9 deposited as F.D. in the name of the SCCH 15 24 MVC No.6392/2018 Petitioner in any Nationalized or Schedule bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
